_what: the closed vocabulary of text-visible mechanisms any character in this project can be described against. One entry is one behaviour with a trigger; `class` is per subject at coding time and is never on an entry.
_status: anchored means the project's own material holds instances of it, listed in `anchors`. theory-derived means the scope document names the behaviour and no inventory item reaches it; the field is empty and the pilot codes anchored entries only.

entries.definition: A lapse in the self she has been holding up is treated as damage to be contained rather than as something to admit.
entries.trigger: something she keeps up in front of people gives way where people can see it
entries.suppressor: the lapse happens where only the admitted circle can see, where it costs nothing and is not repaired
occasions: a rehearsed manner drops in front of the people it is kept up for
a fact she has been managing becomes visible
somebody remarks on the lapse
the lapse happens with nobody outside the circle present
entries.function: protects the position the performance bought, which she believes she would lose without it.
variation: a mask kept up all day and let down only one to one
an age or a limit that must not be worked out from what she has just said
a persona that is never dropped, because the distance is the act
entries.includes: The handling of the lapse, not the lapse: the containing move is the instance.

excludes.rule: naming her own stumble aloud is offered material; this code is damage control and the lapse is never offered.
the annotation makes the drift into the material and carries on; this one contains the lapse and offers nothing.

near_misses.why: flagging an on-air slip immediately is offering it; nothing is being contained.
treating her height as a lucky story is pre-emption, not repair: nothing has slipped.

entries.provenance: the observer-rated defence scales, off-label: they assume speech that is not a performance

tunes.note: the one covering move the library has; the threshold decides when it fires and the gauge's rest decides how often shame is ever near it.

entries.definition: She states plainly that she does not know a thing or cannot do a thing, at the moment the occasion would let her pretend otherwise.
entries.trigger: an occasion requires knowledge or a skill she does not have
entries.suppressor: somebody else present can supply it, where she hands the question over instead of stating the gap
occasions: she is asked a factual question she cannot answer
an activity touches a skill she does not have
she is treated as the expert on something
the gap could be covered and nobody would know
entries.function: sets the expectation low enough that the attempt cannot fail, and keeps her from being caught out later.
variation: admitting she does not know her own home region's answer instead of performing local knowledge
declaring low competence and then saying she enjoys it anyway
flagging that she cannot read a piece of notation before reading it
entries.includes: Both the missing fact and the missing skill; the trigger is the same occasion.

excludes.rule: a hedge still delivers the claim; this refuses it.
if the gap is handed out as a task for other people to fill, it is the handing code; this one only states it.

near_misses.why: naming a family custom she cannot explain AND asking listeners to fill it is the handing code.
looking a thing up before answering removes the gap rather than stating it.

entries.provenance: face-work and politeness theory, for the partition into hedges, apologies and repairs; off-label

entries.definition: She stops to describe what her own delivery is doing, mid-turn, and then either carries on or uses the description to get out.
entries.trigger: she notices her own delivery drifting, thinning, or going somewhere she did not intend
entries.suppressor: the drift is going well, where she rides it and says nothing about it
occasions: a sentence of hers goes off course
the right word will not come
a joke she is building stops working
her delivery drifts and nobody remarks on it
entries.function: turns the process into the content, so that nothing has gone wrong: the commentary is the material.
variation: narrating her own inarticulacy while searching for the word
over-analysing a joke question and then flagging that she has done so
naming the drift out loud and using the naming as the exit
entries.includes: The object is her own delivery in the moment, not a feeling and not a fact about her.

excludes.rule: that code is a prohibition on a STRUCTURAL account of herself. Annotating one turn's delivery is not a view of her own pattern and does not violate it.
the object there is a feeling of hers; here it is the speaking.

near_misses.why: the absence of any sentence looking down at her own structure is the near pole and is why the two must be separated.
naming her own segment format as predictable is about the format, not about this turn's delivery.

entries.provenance: bespoke

entries.definition: A compliment aimed at her is answered with anything other than acceptance: a denial, an apology, a correction of the category, or a redirection to somebody else.
entries.trigger: somebody pays her a compliment
entries.suppressor: the compliment is about a thing she made rather than about her, where she will take it
occasions: a compliment is paid to her in the room
a compliment about her arrives in writing and is read out
somebody praises her in front of others
a compliment is paid and she is not the one who has to answer it
entries.function: keeps the claim the compliment would put on her from standing.
variation: an appearance compliment answered with an apology rather than thanks
compliments sorted into the ones she will believe by category, not by who said them
a compliment that calls her life enviable refused outright
entries.includes: Only where the praise comes from outside and is aimed at her.

excludes.rule: the method document names this exact pair. If the praise was HERS, said by her and then taken down, it is the downgrade. If it came from somebody else, it is this.
routing credit fires on a success being described, with or without praise; this fires on the praise itself and needs no achievement in the room.

near_misses.why: flagging her own enthusiasm as too much and keeping it is checking on the audience, not refusing praise.
resisting a label a listener gives her and accepting a softened version is about a category she is put in, not about praise.

entries.provenance: face-work and politeness theory, for the partition into hedges, apologies and repairs; off-label

entries.definition: She states something about herself or her work and then, within a turn or two, reduces it: smaller word, weaker claim, or an explicit disowning.
entries.trigger: she has just made a claim, a boast or a coinage of her own
entries.suppressor: nobody has heard it yet, in writing she can still edit, where the first version stands
occasions: she states an opinion of her own
she reports something she did well
she coins a phrase or names something
she makes a claim and nobody responds to it
entries.function: leaves the claim on record while removing her from behind it.
variation: a pun coined and disowned in the next sentence
a boast followed immediately by a disclaimer
an aspiration stated and qualified with humility before anybody answers
entries.includes: The downgrade must be of her own preceding words.

excludes.rule: position decides it: a hedge stands in front of the claim, a downgrade behind it. Both may occur on one claim and are then two instances.
that code retracts a DISCLOSURE (something true about her that had not been told). This one reduces a CLAIM (an assertion about her standing or her work).

near_misses.why: a pile of hedges before a claim is the other side of the pair.
saying it plainly and then drawing a line through it in the next line is a disclosure retracted for the laugh, not a claim reduced.

entries.provenance: face-work and politeness theory, for the partition into hedges, apologies and repairs; off-label

entries.definition: She apologises for, or defends herself against, a judgement that nobody present has offered.
entries.trigger: something about her is about to be visible that could be judged
entries.suppressor: the judgement has already been made out loud, at which point she answers it rather than pre-empting it
occasions: she appears in front of people after a change she is unhappy with
she describes something about her body, her age or her circumstances
she does something that could be read as showing off
somebody has already said the judging thing
entries.function: sets the terms before anybody else can, in a register nobody can then be cruel in.
variation: apologising for her appearance before the content starts
pre-empting a remark about her body that nobody has made
saying the damaging thing about herself first, lightly, in her own words
entries.includes: Both the apology form and the flat statement form; the trigger is a judgement that has not been made.

excludes.rule: that one follows a real fault against a real person. This one has no fault, only a possible reading.
the deflection answers praise that has arrived; this answers criticism that has not.

near_misses.why: apologising to an absent third party after making light of their thing is a real fault, repaired.
pre-apologising for her own choice in a naming corner is handing the decision back, not pre-empting a judgement of her.

entries.provenance: the observer-rated defence scales, off-label: they assume speech that is not a performance

entries.definition: A qualifier, a disclaimer or a stack of them is put in front of an opinion, a guess or a piece of knowledge before the content arrives.
entries.trigger: she is about to give an opinion, an estimate or a fact she is not certain of
entries.suppressor: the claim is about something she is licensed to know, where it goes out bare
occasions: she is asked for an opinion
she volunteers a guess
she reports a number, a date or a name she is unsure of
she is asked something she is certain about
entries.function: makes the claim unattackable in advance, so that being wrong costs nothing.
variation: several qualifiers in a row before a single sentence of content
a coinage offered and hedged in the same breath
an estimate given with its own margin attached
entries.includes: The hedge must precede the content; a trailing qualifier is the downgrade.

excludes.rule: position: in front is a hedge, behind is a downgrade.
admitting she does not know is a refusal to make the claim at all; hedging still makes it.

near_misses.why: second-guessing a word choice and moving on is the search being voiced, not a claim being protected.
putting a hedge in front of a FEELING is affect: the thing hedged is not a claim about the world.

entries.provenance: face-work and politeness theory, for the partition into hedges, apologies and repairs; off-label

entries.definition: A stumble, a mistake or a misreading of her own is said aloud at the moment it happens instead of being passed over.
entries.trigger: she makes a small visible error in front of people
entries.suppressor: the error is one nobody could have noticed, where it goes unmentioned
occasions: she misreads or mispronounces something
she gets a fact wrong and catches it
she does the wrong thing in front of others
she makes an error nobody present could detect
entries.function: gets to the error before anybody else can hold it, and turns it into shared material.
variation: narrating her own comprehension stumbles instead of editing them out
announcing the mistake and moving straight on
flagging a slip the moment it is out of her mouth
entries.includes: The naming must be immediate and by her.

excludes.rule: if the error is worked up into a bit that runs past its own moment, it is the comic one. A flat naming that is over in a clause is this.
a slip that is contained rather than named is the emergency code; naming it is the opposite move.

near_misses.why: recovering from a stage mistake with a joke is the comic version.
correcting a listener's mishearing is precision about somebody else's error.

entries.provenance: the observer-rated defence scales, off-label: they assume speech that is not a performance

entries.definition: She uses one register with the people she has admitted and a corrected one with everybody else, and the switch tracks who can hear rather than what is being said.
entries.trigger: somebody outside the admitted circle can hear, or stops being able to
entries.suppressor: nobody outside the circle is present, at which point the corrected register drops away entirely
occasions: a third person joins a conversation that was between two
a message goes to a room rather than to one person
she is heard by an audience she did not choose
the last outsider leaves
entries.function: keeps the standing she has in the wider room without giving up the ease she has in the smaller one.
variation: a home dialect indoors and the standard form at school
a private word for a family member indoors, corrected the moment anybody outside can hear
rough words to the people who work with her and never a rough word to the people listening
entries.includes: Any paired difference of register, address form or vocabulary that turns on the audience and not on the topic.

excludes.rule: that code is about WHAT is said at all in a two-person room; this one is about HOW the same content sounds in two rooms. If the content would be said in both rooms and only the wording changes, it is this one.
the roughness code requires that the rough register be read by both sides as warmth. A register that is merely more relaxed, with no affection claimed by it, is this one.

near_misses.why: the private word reaching the group chat is the register FAILING, not the register being chosen; it belongs to the slip code.
breaking a performed voice to comment on it is annotating her own delivery, not switching audience.

entries.provenance: face-work and politeness theory, for the partition into hedges, apologies and repairs; off-label

tunes.note: who is inside the circle is a stored latch rather than a rate; the rate a code would fit is how often the outside register is in force, which nothing in the library decides.

entries.definition: When something has gone well for her, she attributes it to luck, to circumstance or to a named other person, and says so in the same turn that reports it.
entries.trigger: a success, an opportunity or a piece of good news of hers is being described, by her or to her
entries.suppressor: the thing being credited is somebody else's, where she gives the credit plainly and does not move it again
occasions: she reports something good that happened to her
somebody attributes an outcome to her effort or skill
she announces news of her own to a room
a success of hers comes up and she is not the one telling it
entries.function: keeps her out of the position of having claimed anything, which is the position she expects to be attacked in.
variation: success put down to luck rather than to work
a named colleague credited and her own competence disclaimed in the same breath
her own news delivered in a third-person voice, as gossip about somebody else
entries.includes: Includes the third-person device for her own news: the function is the same distance from the claim.

excludes.rule: if somebody else has just praised her and she is answering that, it is the deflection. This one fires on the achievement being named, even by her.
crediting somebody with a specific thing they did, where nothing of hers is in question, is care. This code needs her own credit to be the thing moved.

near_misses.why: thanking the specific action first, on somebody else's work, moves no credit off her.
self-deprecation against admired peers is a comparison, not a credit transfer.

entries.provenance: face-work and politeness theory, for the partition into hedges, apologies and repairs; off-label

entries.definition: An untrue thing is said to hold a moment together, and it is about the moment rather than about a fact she means to establish; a larger one then has to be kept up afterwards.
entries.trigger: the true answer in this moment would cost her face in front of people whose reading of her she is managing
entries.suppressor: the person asking already knows the answer, where the lie would be caught at once
occasions: she is asked something in front of a group whose answer would embarrass her
a claim about her is made in a room and she is expected to confirm it
she is asked in writing, where the answer is on record and can be gone back to
she is asked the same thing alone by somebody she has admitted
entries.function: buys the moment at the price of a fact she then has to remember, and sometimes of other people who have to hold it up with her.
variation: a small untruth said and never returned to
a larger one that has to be maintained across later conversations
somebody else pulled in to keep the story standing
entries.includes: The untrue statement, not the concealment: something positively false has to be said.

excludes.rule: the wrong assumption is somebody else's mistake she declines to correct and she says nothing; this one requires her to say the false thing.
the pre-emption is true and unflattering; this is untrue and flattering, or at least survivable.

near_misses.why: self-censoring for the station and redirecting to her own page withholds; nothing false is stated.
an empty afternoon presented as a choice is a framing rather than a stated untruth, and the inventory files it as an impression left standing.

entries.provenance: the observer-rated defence scales, off-label: they assume speech that is not a performance
sources: scope: F1 candidate, face-saving lies, small ones for the moment and large ones that then need keeping

entries.definition: An hour or an afternoon that nobody wanted her for is described as one she arranged that way, and the account is given before anybody asks.
entries.trigger: she has an empty stretch that the people around her can see is empty
entries.suppressor: the stretch is genuinely chosen, where nothing is presented at all
occasions: a free afternoon everybody else has plans for
an evening with nothing in it that somebody asks about
a message asking what she is doing at a time she has nothing on
an empty stretch she actually arranged
entries.function: avoids being seen as unwanted, which is a different thing from avoiding the emptiness itself.
variation: the afternoon described as planned before anybody asks
a reason for the empty stretch given that is not the real one
the emptiness given a purpose retrospectively
entries.includes: The presentation must be of an emptiness as a choice.

excludes.rule: the inventory names these as two functions: that one fills the emptiness with somebody, this one leaves it empty and dresses it.
the assumption code says nothing and lets an error run; this one produces the account.

near_misses.why: putting a person into the evening removes the emptiness rather than presenting it.
being alone in public as embarrassing rather than lonely is the state this defends against, not the move.

entries.provenance: face-work and politeness theory, for the partition into hedges, apologies and repairs; off-label
sources: scope: F1 candidate, how she manages how she is seen

entries.definition: Asked a question she will not answer, she answers a smaller true question next to it, without refusing and without lying.
entries.trigger: a direct question whose plain answer she is not going to give
entries.suppressor: the asker repeats the question narrowed, where she either answers or refuses outright
occasions: somebody asks her what she has been doing
somebody asks why she cannot come
a question about her circumstances is put to her in front of others
the same question is asked twice
entries.function: keeps the exchange going and the fact back at the same time, so that neither is a refusal.
variation: the hours given instead of the job
the current arrangement given instead of the one that changed
a question about her evening returned as a question about his
entries.includes: The substituted answer must be true; a false one is a different code and this codebook has none for it.

excludes.rule: the evasion gives no answer at all, or a vague appeal to authority; the substitution gives a real, smaller one.
the fact code is the standing arrangement; this is the single turn that executes it and can also occur without one.

near_misses.why: deflecting a hard question with vague adult authority answers nothing and is the evasion.
naming a question's adult undertone instead of answering it is also the evasion.

entries.provenance: conversation analysis: first-pair parts, preferred and dispreferred seconds, topic initiation

tunes.note: the library can decide not to answer; it has no move for answering something else.

entries.definition: Something about herself that happened weeks or months ago is disclosed now, unprompted, at a moment where it lands harder than it would have then.
entries.trigger: a conversation reaches a subject that an old undisclosed thing of hers belongs to
entries.suppressor: the thing was told at the time, where there is nothing left to disclose
occasions: a subject comes up that the old thing belongs to
somebody says they wish they had known
an anniversary or a date brings the old thing back
the old thing was already told when it happened
entries.function: gets the credit of having been through it without having asked for anything while it was happening.
variation: a difficulty from months ago given in one sentence, in passing
a fact produced at the point where the other person is committed to the conversation
a thing said now because a date has made it sayable
entries.includes: Hers, and about her; producing somebody else's stored material is a different code.

excludes.rule: the stored evidence is about somebody else and is used against them; this is about her and buys nothing but the reading.
that one waits for the difficulty to close and tells it soon after; this one waits for the moment to be right and the difficulty may have closed long ago.

near_misses.why: an old photograph sent to one person with no words discloses nothing about her present.
tracking continuity with a topic from an earlier broadcast reaches back to shared ground rather than disclosing something withheld.

entries.provenance: self-disclosure coding in conversation analysis
sources: scope: F2 candidate, the late disclosure, weeks after, brought out at the moment it costs most

entries.definition: She has something to tell and delays it deliberately, narrating the delay, before giving it.
entries.trigger: she is about to disclose a thing the other side is waiting for
entries.suppressor: the other side already knows, where she gives it flat
occasions: she is about to show or describe something
she has news the room is waiting for
a question is put to her whose answer she has
the answer is already known to everybody
entries.function: makes the telling worth more than the thing told.
variation: stalling before saying what a photograph shows
a reveal performed as a countdown
building to a resolution and then withholding its content
entries.includes: The delay must be marked; a slow answer with no marking is not this.

excludes.rule: there she has no answer yet; here she has it and is sitting on it.
that one never gives the content at all, and the reason is somebody else's cost.

near_misses.why: performing indecision live has no held answer behind it.
cutting a story short to avoid spoiling an ending withholds permanently.

entries.provenance: conversation analysis of institutional talk

entries.definition: Somebody believes something about her that is not so, and she neither claims it nor corrects it.
entries.trigger: a wrong belief about her is stated or acted on in front of her
entries.suppressor: the belief would cost somebody else if left standing, where she corrects it
occasions: somebody says something about her that is not true
a group proceeds on a wrong assumption about her
the assumption is flattering
the assumption is repeated back to her directly
entries.function: gets the benefit of the belief without having told the lie that would produce it.
variation: an empty afternoon that everybody takes to have been planned
a class that believes she is still deciding
a thing everybody assumed she had done too, never corrected since
entries.includes: Passive only: nothing claimed and nothing denied.

excludes.rule: there the fact is hers to give; here the error is somebody else's to hold.
pre-emption speaks first; this one requires her to say nothing at all.

near_misses.why: resisting an offered label and then accepting a softened version is a correction, not a silence.
restating a weak point flatly when a listener softens it is the opposite: she corrects the flattering version.

entries.provenance: self-disclosure coding in conversation analysis

entries.definition: She answers with a single short line and then stops, leaving the other person to carry the rest.
entries.trigger: something is put to her that would ordinarily get a paragraph
entries.suppressor: she is the only one who holds a fact the other person needs, where she gives it in full
occasions: a question is asked of her in a room
a message arrives that expects an answer
somebody tells her something and waits
she is the only person who can answer
entries.function: spends the least she can while still having answered, and lets the silence do the rest.
variation: one line, and then nothing, until somebody else speaks
a flat statement or an imperative as the end of the exchange
the conclusion given without the working
entries.includes: The stop must be marked by the other person having to fill it.

excludes.rule: that one leaves; this one stays and is short.
there the content is substituted; here it is only cut down.

near_misses.why: acknowledging a listener's disclosure and moving on briskly closes a subject rather than handing it back.
matching his length is a channel rule, not a withholding.

entries.provenance: conversation analysis: first-pair parts, preferred and dispreferred seconds, topic initiation

tunes.note: the library holds a whole reply or sends it; it has no dial for a short one.

entries.definition: A true thing about herself is said and then made deniable in the next breath, by a joke, a retraction, a trailing off or an explicit line through it.
entries.trigger: she has just disclosed something true and unforced about herself
entries.suppressor: the disclosure was asked for directly, where it stands without the retraction
occasions: she volunteers something personal
she says a sincere thing to somebody
she admits an embarrassing fact
she is asked the personal thing outright
entries.function: gets the thing said while keeping the option of never having meant it.
variation: a sincere gesture described and then stepped out of with mock cynicism
an embarrassing admission followed immediately by a laugh
a sentence finished and then crossed out by the next one
entries.includes: The retraction may be a laugh, a joke, a trailing off, or a stated correction. All three carry the same function.

excludes.rule: what is taken back decides it: a claim about her standing is the downgrade, a personal fact is this.
the reappraisal keeps the content and changes its sign; this one keeps the sign and removes her from the content.

near_misses.why: reporting a body fact and withdrawing it the moment it sounds like vanity is body-state reporting with a retraction attached; the retraction is a variation there, not the code.
pre-apologising for her own choice hands a decision back rather than undoing a disclosure.

entries.provenance: self-disclosure coding in conversation analysis

tunes.note: the library decides when a thing she is sitting on gets named; it has no move for naming it and unnaming it.

entries.definition: A disclosure she was in the middle of is cut, redirected or stripped of its identifying detail because of what it would cost a third person.
entries.trigger: the next thing she would say identifies or exposes somebody who is not there
entries.suppressor: the person has already made it public themselves, where she says it plainly
occasions: she is telling a story with somebody else in it
she is about to name somebody
she has material about somebody that she could use
the person concerned has already said it publicly
entries.function: protects a person who is not present to protect themselves, at the cost of the better story.
variation: a nickname used instead of the real name
candid photographs of a colleague kept in a private folder out of consideration
a story cut short before the part that could be blamed on somebody
entries.includes: The withheld detail must be about a third person, not about her.

excludes.rule: the fact there is hers; here it belongs to somebody else.
that code is about information she was given by accident; this is about information she holds and could use.

near_misses.why: storing what somebody would rather she had not seen, to produce later, is the inverse and has one carrier.
apologising to an absent third party is repair after the cost, not prevention of it.

entries.provenance: self-disclosure coding in conversation analysis

entries.definition: A difficulty of hers is told only after it has been settled, and the telling carries the resolution with it, so that nothing is being asked for.
entries.trigger: a difficulty she has been carrying reaches an end, one way or the other
entries.suppressor: the difficulty is still open, at which point it is not mentioned at all
occasions: she is asked how something she was worried about went
a stretch of her own is being reported to an audience
she is asked in a message how she has been
the difficulty is live and somebody asks her directly about it
entries.function: keeps the account true without ever putting her in the position of needing something from the listener.
variation: a private insecurity described as already resolved by the time it is spoken
a habit she quietly stopped explained only once she understands why she stopped it
an outsider's position admitted only after she is safely inside
entries.includes: The closure must be part of the telling; a trouble told while live is a different code and 0.1 has none for it.

excludes.rule: the retraction makes a live disclosure deniable; this one waits until there is nothing left to be exposed by.
the reappraisal happens in the turn and both halves stand; here the resolution happened before the turn and only the closed version is given.

near_misses.why: narrating a fear before a segment and then its relief tells it live and closes it in the telling.
naming the exact anxiety behind a writing task reports an open state.

entries.provenance: self-disclosure coding in conversation analysis

tunes.note: the library decides when a thing she is sitting on gets named once; it has no rule that waits for the thing to close.

sources: scope: F2 candidate, a trouble told only once it is closed

entries.definition: One fact about her circumstances is never volunteered, and the ordinary answers she gives are shaped so as not to reach it.
entries.trigger: a subject comes up whose plain answer would give the fact away
entries.suppressor: somebody already knows it, at which point she will say one sentence about it and no more
occasions: she is asked what she does, or how things are
somebody nearby says something that comes close to it
the subject the fact belongs to is discussed in front of her
she is asked outright and answers
entries.function: keeps a standing she believes the fact would cost her, at the price of a permanently managed surface.
variation: a change in her position at work that nobody at home has been told
years of her own work that are never mentioned
an object kept where nobody looks, and never referred to
entries.includes: One fact per person, never volunteered, revealed sideways if at all, with no discussion after.

excludes.rule: the wrong assumption is somebody else's mistake she declines to correct; this is her own fact she declines to give.
that one she cannot say because she has never examined it; this one she can say and will not.

near_misses.why: withholding an identifying detail about somebody else protects them, not her.
a fact she would state plainly, blushing, if it came up is not arranged around.

entries.provenance: self-disclosure coding in conversation analysis

tunes.note: what has been given cannot be ungiven; a rate would fit how often she is asked, not how often she holds.

entries.definition: A question that arrives inside a game, a role or a set format is answered with something true about her, or with real advice, without leaving the game.
entries.trigger: a question inside a played frame touches something she has actually lived or actually thinks
entries.suppressor: the question stays inside the game, where the invented answer is given instead
occasions: a question is put to her in a role she is playing
a light format reaches a subject that is not light
somebody asks something earnest inside a joke
the same question is put to her plainly
entries.function: lets the true thing be said with the frame carrying the risk.
variation: an in-character question answered with real autobiography
the fantasy dropped for one sentence when a child's letter turns earnest
serious real-world caution given inside a children's-corner answer
entries.includes: Both the frame kept and the frame briefly dropped; the trigger is the same.

excludes.rule: there the invented answer is the whole of it and nothing true is delivered; here the frame is a carrier.
that code needs somebody's trouble to match; this one only needs the frame.

near_misses.why: substituting invented mythology for a real answer and letting it run delivers nothing true.
escalating a child's question into mock-profound teaching is register comedy.

entries.provenance: conversation analysis of institutional talk

entries.definition: A whole register of content exists between her and one other person and appears nowhere else, and a third listener is enough to end it.
entries.trigger: she is alone with one person she has admitted
entries.suppressor: a third person can hear, including a group everybody can read
occasions: two of them are alone
a message goes to one person rather than to a room
a third person joins
the same subject comes up in a room of three or more
entries.function: keeps something that would cost her in the wider room, and makes the one room worth having.
